title: GCSE Chemistry diagnostic
summary: 16 multiple-choice questions across atomic structure, bonding, quantitative chemistry, reactions, rates, organic chemistry and analysis.

questions.question: An atom has 11 protons and 12 neutrons. What is its mass number?
questions.explanation: The mass number is the total number of protons and neutrons in the nucleus: 11 + 12 = 23. The number of protons alone, 11, is the atomic number.

questions.question: Why does the reactivity of the Group 1 metals increase going down the group?
options: The atoms have more outer electrons
The atoms get smaller, so the nucleus attracts electrons more strongly
The metals become harder to melt
The outer electron is further from the nucleus, so it is lost more easily
questions.explanation: Going down Group 1 the atoms have more electron shells. The single outer electron is further from the nucleus and more shielded, so it is attracted less strongly and lost more easily.

questions.question: Why does sodium chloride have a high melting point?
options: It is made of small molecules with weak forces between them
There are strong electrostatic forces between oppositely charged ions in a giant lattice
It contains delocalised electrons that are free to move
Each atom is joined to four others by covalent bonds
questions.explanation: Sodium chloride is a giant ionic lattice. A lot of energy is needed to overcome the strong electrostatic attraction between the positive sodium ions and negative chloride ions.

questions.question: What is the relative formula mass of calcium carbonate, $\text{CaCO}_3$? (Relative atomic masses: Ca = 40, C = 12, O = 16)
questions.explanation: Add the masses of every atom in the formula: $40 + 12 + (3 \times 16) = 100$.

questions.question: What is the mass of $0.25$ moles of carbon dioxide, $\text{CO}_2$? (Relative atomic masses: C = 12, O = 16)
questions.explanation: The relative formula mass of $\text{CO}_2$ is $12 + (2 \times 16) = 44$. Mass = moles $\times$ formula mass $= 0.25 \times 44 = 11$ g.

questions.question: What are the products when an acid reacts with a metal carbonate?
options: A salt, water and carbon dioxide
A metal oxide and carbon dioxide
questions.explanation: Acid + metal carbonate gives a salt, water and carbon dioxide. A salt and hydrogen are made when an acid reacts with a metal, and a salt and water when it reacts with an alkali.

questions.question: Molten lead bromide is electrolysed. What forms at the negative electrode (cathode)?
questions.explanation: Positive lead ions are attracted to the negative electrode, where they gain electrons and form lead metal. Bromine forms at the positive electrode. There is no water present, so no hydrogen or oxygen forms.

questions.question: Which statement describes an exothermic reaction?
options: Energy is transferred to the surroundings, so the temperature of the surroundings rises
Energy is taken in from the surroundings, so the temperature of the surroundings falls
No energy is transferred during the reaction
The products always have more energy than the reactants
questions.explanation: An exothermic reaction transfers energy to the surroundings, so the surroundings get warmer. The products end up with less energy than the reactants.

questions.question: Why does increasing the temperature increase the rate of a reaction?
options: The particles move faster, so they collide more often and with more energy
There are more particles in the same volume
questions.explanation: At a higher temperature the particles have more energy and move faster. They collide more often, and more of the collisions have at least the activation energy, so more are successful.

questions.question: In the reaction $\text{N}_2 + 3\text{H}_2 \rightleftharpoons 2\text{NH}_3$ the forward reaction is exothermic. What happens to the yield of ammonia if the temperature is increased?
questions.explanation: Raising the temperature moves the equilibrium in the endothermic direction to oppose the change. Here that is the reverse reaction, so less ammonia is present at equilibrium.

questions.question: What is the general formula of the alkanes?
questions.explanation: Alkanes are saturated hydrocarbons with the general formula $\text{C}_n\text{H}_{2n+2}$, for example methane $\text{CH}_4$ and ethane $\text{C}_2\text{H}_6$. $\text{C}_n\text{H}_{2n}$ is the formula for alkenes.

questions.question: Bromine water is shaken with an alkene. What colour change is seen?
questions.explanation: Alkenes have a carbon to carbon double bond that reacts with bromine, so orange bromine water turns colourless. With an alkane it would stay orange.

questions.question: In a chromatography experiment a spot of dye moves $3.6\ \text{cm}$ and the solvent front moves $8.0\ \text{cm}$. What is the $R_f$ value of the dye?
questions.explanation: $R_f$ is the distance moved by the substance divided by the distance moved by the solvent: $3.6 \div 8.0 = 0.45$. An $R_f$ value is always less than $1$.

questions.question: A compound gives a lilac flame in a flame test. Which metal ion does it contain?
questions.explanation: Potassium ions give a lilac flame. Sodium gives yellow, calcium gives orange-red and copper gives green.

questions.question: Which gas makes up about four-fifths of the Earth's atmosphere today?
questions.explanation: The atmosphere is about 78% nitrogen, roughly four-fifths. Oxygen makes up about 21%, with small amounts of argon, carbon dioxide and other gases.

questions.question: What does it mean when water is described as potable?
options: It contains no dissolved substances at all
questions.explanation: Potable water is water that is safe to drink. It is not chemically pure: it still contains low levels of dissolved salts, but harmful microbes have been removed or killed.
